newsitem.title: ITALY: Iraq says Agip close to deal on Nasiriya.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Agip close to deal on Nasiriya.

text.p: Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Thursday that he had held talks with Italian energy group ENI and its subsidiary Agip and was close to a deal on development of the Nasiriya oil field.
"We have reached a very advanced stage. We hope to settle in the coming weeks...We are in almost full agreement," Rasheed told a news conference in Rome.
Rasheed said Agip was planning to invest $2 billion in the development of the field if the deal went ahead.

He said the concession would be valid for about 23 years, adding he expected production for the field to reach 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) after around four years and revenue to be $2 billion per year.
"The investment is near to two billion dollars. It is a very important oil field," he said.

Rasheed said, however, that Iraq wanted political support for the ending of United Nations sanctions in force since the 1990 invasion of Kuwait. "We have to find the right political climate," he said.
Rasheed said he held talks on Wednesday with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and said Italy was "moving in the right direction".
